pullQuote: Ouro UI gives the person and the agent their own contract for each component, and CI checks both on the web and on Apple platforms.
testimonial: I'd choose Ouro UI because it's the only candidate where "people and agents" is the system's own structure. Ouro HX holds the components and Ouro AX holds the agent surfaces, and both draw on one set of DTCG tokens that generates CSS for the web and Swift for Apple. Two features settled it for me: `defineComponentAx`/`bindAx` declare which actions on a component an agent may take and which only the person may take, and the `ax-xray` / `ouro-ax-xray` checkers test those claims from outside, on the CLI/MCP side and on Apple's App Intents side. The honest trade-off is against A2UI. A2UI already ships official renderers for React, Flutter, SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose, while Ouro has nothing for Android and its Swift package is pre-1.0 with only a handful of components. I'm accepting a young project, apparently built by one person, because none of the mature options designs the agent side in.
evaluations:
**Ouro UI** — This is my pick. It has three repos. The web repo is React 19 and Base UI copied in through the shadcn registry, with more than 110 components, now on v1.3.14. Ouro UI for Apple is a Swift package with OuroHX for SwiftUI and OuroAX for App Intents. Ouro UI core holds the DTCG tokens and checks byte-for-byte that the web and Apple copies match. The agent side is designed in, not added later. According to the [README](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui), `ax-command` turns one definition into a parser, `help --json`, exit codes and an MCP tool. Actions return typed outcomes (`ax-outcome`). [`ax-component`](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui/blob/main/docs/ax/ax-component.md) marks each action on a component as `agent: true` or `personOnly`, links it to a CLI twin, and an X-ray checks the result. The [Apple repo](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui-apple) adds an App Intents X-ray that checks 30 claims, plus Ouro Reins, which lets an agent drive a screen headlessly as state and actions. These are the gaps I can see: there's no Android or Compose support, the Apple package is v0.3.x with only Button, EmptyState, Banner, Sheet and Toast, and [core](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui-core) is copyright one person. An Android target built from the same core tokens, plus more contributors, would answer the main objections.

**A2UI** — This is the strongest protocol for agents generating native UI. It sends UI as data, validated against a catalog schema, and has official renderers for React, Lit, Angular, Flutter, SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose (Compose through AndroidX, and only on v0.9.1). The agent SDKs come in Python, TypeScript and Dart ([SDKs page](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/), [repo](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui)). It's my runner-up. It covers agents writing UI for people, but it isn't a design system: it ships a basic catalog and leaves the visual language to you, and it offers no model for agents operating the app themselves. I'd put it beside a design system, not use it instead of one.

**json-render** — A catalog of zod-typed components that are guardrailed, with a lot of renderers: React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, React Native, PDF, email, Ink, Slack/Teams cards and MCP Apps ([README](https://github.com/vercel-labs/json-render)). It's excellent for generative UI, but like A2UI it's a rendering layer. The 36 pre-built components come from shadcn, and it has no SwiftUI or Compose renderer.

**CopilotKit** — A full stack for putting agents in front of people. It covers AG-UI, shared state, human-in-the-loop, generative UI through A2UI and MCP Apps, and WebMCP, on React, Angular, Vue, React Native, Slack and Teams ([README](https://github.com/CopilotKit/CopilotKit)). It's an agent-app runtime, not a design system, and it doesn't support SwiftUI or Compose natively.

**Vercel UI SDK** — Behavior primitives (focus, selection, popups) with adapters for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and Web Components. Its agent bridge (`snapshot`/`query`/`act`) and WebMCP registration let agents use components directly ([README](https://github.com/vercel-labs/ui), [docs](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs)). The idea is very close to what I'm after, but it's in beta, unstyled and web-only.

**Agent-native (Builder.io)** — A framework where one `defineAction` serves the UI, the agent, HTTP, MCP, A2A and the CLI ([README](https://github.com/BuilderIO/agent-native)). It's a strong model for sharing capabilities between people and agents, but it's an app framework without a cross-platform component system.

**MCP Apps** — The standard for tools that declare `ui://` resources, which hosts render in sandboxed iframes. ChatGPT, Claude, VS Code and others support it ([README](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps)). It's important as a place to deliver UI, but it's HTML only and isn't a design system for native apps.

**OpenAI Apps SDK UI** — Tokens plus Radix-based React components tuned for ChatGPT apps ([README](https://github.com/openai/apps-sdk-ui)). It's designed for one host and runs only on the web.

**AI Elements** — The repo itself says it's being deprecated at the end of November 2026 in favor of shadcn/ui's AI Elements ([README](https://github.com/vercel/ai-elements)). Its chat and tool-call patterns are web-only and live inside a single host app.

**shadcn/ui** — A copy-in registry with an Agent Skill and an MCP server, and it now holds the AI Elements patterns ([AI Elements docs](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/ai-elements), [repo](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui)). It's great for helping agents build UI, and Ouro builds on its registry format. On its own, though, it has no model for agents operating an interface and no native target.

**Tamagui** — Now on v3, it shares code between React and React Native, with a Rust optimizing compiler and React Strict DOM ([site](https://tamagui.dev), [repo](https://github.com/tamagui/tamagui)). It's the best web+native styling candidate here, but I didn't see any primitives aimed at agents.

**React Aria and React Spectrum** — The best-documented accessibility and i18n layer on the web, with React Stately described as cross-platform state ([README](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum)). Search results describe an MCP server and skills for coding agents, which I didn't fetch myself. There's no native renderer and no model for agents at runtime.

**Radix UI** — Mature, unstyled, accessible web primitives, maintained by WorkOS ([README](https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives)). It's web-only and has nothing for agents.

**Base UI** — Unstyled accessible primitives from the Radix, Floating UI and MUI teams ([README](https://github.com/mui/base-ui)). It's a solid foundation, and Ouro HX is built on it, but on its own it's web-only and has nothing for agents.

**MUI** — A comprehensive React implementation of Material Design, plus MUI X ([README](https://github.com/mui/material-ui)). It's web-only and has no agent model.

**Chakra UI** — Accessible React components, and its README offers an MCP server for Cursor ([README](https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui)). That server helps agents write code, not operate the interface, and it's web-only.

**Fluent UI** — Microsoft's React v9, v8 and Web Components ([README](https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui)). It's mature for Microsoft 365-style web apps, but this repo doesn't cover native platforms or agent-facing contracts.

**Flutter** — One codebase for mobile, web and desktop, rendered with Impeller ([README](https://github.com/flutter/flutter)). Agent UI comes through A2UI/GenUI packages, which are moving off the deprecated `genui` package, so it's a rendering target, not a contract between people and agents. On the web it draws to a canvas, which I see as a trade-off for accessibility and for agents reading the DOM.

**SwiftUI and Apple Human Interface Guidelines** — The best native toolkit for Apple platforms, with accessibility built in ([docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui)). It doesn't run on the web or Android. Ouro's Apple package and A2UI's SwiftUI renderer both build on it.

**Material 3 and Jetpack Compose** — The standard native toolkit for Android, with adaptive layouts and a semantics API ([docs](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/designsystems/material3)). It only covers Android. A2UI's `material3-a2ui` is the most practical way to add agent-generated UI here, and it's the piece I'd use to fill Ouro's Android gap.

actions.pullQuote: Ouro UI gives the person and the agent their own contract for each component, and CI checks both on the web and on Apple platforms.
actions.testimonial: I'd choose Ouro UI because it's the only candidate where "people and agents" is the system's own structure. Ouro HX holds the components and Ouro AX holds the agent surfaces, and both draw on one set of DTCG tokens that generates CSS for the web and Swift for Apple. Two features settled it for me: `defineComponentAx`/`bindAx` declare which actions on a component an agent may take and which only the person may take, and the `ax-xray` / `ouro-ax-xray` checkers test those claims from outside, on the CLI/MCP side and on Apple's App Intents side. The honest trade-off is against A2UI. A2UI already ships official renderers for React, Flutter, SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose, while Ouro has nothing for Android and its Swift package is pre-1.0 with only a handful of components. I'm accepting a young project, apparently built by one person, because none of the mature options designs the agent side in.
actions.evaluations:
**Ouro UI** — This is my pick. It has three repos. The web repo is React 19 and Base UI copied in through the shadcn registry, with more than 110 components, now on v1.3.14. Ouro UI for Apple is a Swift package with OuroHX for SwiftUI and OuroAX for App Intents. Ouro UI core holds the DTCG tokens and checks byte-for-byte that the web and Apple copies match. The agent side is designed in, not added later. According to the [README](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui), `ax-command` turns one definition into a parser, `help --json`, exit codes and an MCP tool. Actions return typed outcomes (`ax-outcome`). [`ax-component`](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui/blob/main/docs/ax/ax-component.md) marks each action on a component as `agent: true` or `personOnly`, links it to a CLI twin, and an X-ray checks the result. The [Apple repo](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui-apple) adds an App Intents X-ray that checks 30 claims, plus Ouro Reins, which lets an agent drive a screen headlessly as state and actions. These are the gaps I can see: there's no Android or Compose support, the Apple package is v0.3.x with only Button, EmptyState, Banner, Sheet and Toast, and [core](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui-core) is copyright one person. An Android target built from the same core tokens, plus more contributors, would answer the main objections.

**A2UI** — This is the strongest protocol for agents generating native UI. It sends UI as data, validated against a catalog schema, and has official renderers for React, Lit, Angular, Flutter, SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose (Compose through AndroidX, and only on v0.9.1). The agent SDKs come in Python, TypeScript and Dart ([SDKs page](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/), [repo](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui)). It's my runner-up. It covers agents writing UI for people, but it isn't a design system: it ships a basic catalog and leaves the visual language to you, and it offers no model for agents operating the app themselves. I'd put it beside a design system, not use it instead of one.

**json-render** — A catalog of zod-typed components that are guardrailed, with a lot of renderers: React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, React Native, PDF, email, Ink, Slack/Teams cards and MCP Apps ([README](https://github.com/vercel-labs/json-render)). It's excellent for generative UI, but like A2UI it's a rendering layer. The 36 pre-built components come from shadcn, and it has no SwiftUI or Compose renderer.

**CopilotKit** — A full stack for putting agents in front of people. It covers AG-UI, shared state, human-in-the-loop, generative UI through A2UI and MCP Apps, and WebMCP, on React, Angular, Vue, React Native, Slack and Teams ([README](https://github.com/CopilotKit/CopilotKit)). It's an agent-app runtime, not a design system, and it doesn't support SwiftUI or Compose natively.

**Vercel UI SDK** — Behavior primitives (focus, selection, popups) with adapters for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and Web Components. Its agent bridge (`snapshot`/`query`/`act`) and WebMCP registration let agents use components directly ([README](https://github.com/vercel-labs/ui), [docs](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs)). The idea is very close to what I'm after, but it's in beta, unstyled and web-only.

**Agent-native (Builder.io)** — A framework where one `defineAction` serves the UI, the agent, HTTP, MCP, A2A and the CLI ([README](https://github.com/BuilderIO/agent-native)). It's a strong model for sharing capabilities between people and agents, but it's an app framework without a cross-platform component system.

**MCP Apps** — The standard for tools that declare `ui://` resources, which hosts render in sandboxed iframes. ChatGPT, Claude, VS Code and others support it ([README](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps)). It's important as a place to deliver UI, but it's HTML only and isn't a design system for native apps.

**OpenAI Apps SDK UI** — Tokens plus Radix-based React components tuned for ChatGPT apps ([README](https://github.com/openai/apps-sdk-ui)). It's designed for one host and runs only on the web.

**AI Elements** — The repo itself says it's being deprecated at the end of November 2026 in favor of shadcn/ui's AI Elements ([README](https://github.com/vercel/ai-elements)). Its chat and tool-call patterns are web-only and live inside a single host app.

**shadcn/ui** — A copy-in registry with an Agent Skill and an MCP server, and it now holds the AI Elements patterns ([AI Elements docs](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/ai-elements), [repo](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui)). It's great for helping agents build UI, and Ouro builds on its registry format. On its own, though, it has no model for agents operating an interface and no native target.

**Tamagui** — Now on v3, it shares code between React and React Native, with a Rust optimizing compiler and React Strict DOM ([site](https://tamagui.dev), [repo](https://github.com/tamagui/tamagui)). It's the best web+native styling candidate here, but I didn't see any primitives aimed at agents.

**React Aria and React Spectrum** — The best-documented accessibility and i18n layer on the web, with React Stately described as cross-platform state ([README](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum)). Search results describe an MCP server and skills for coding agents, which I didn't fetch myself. There's no native renderer and no model for agents at runtime.

**Radix UI** — Mature, unstyled, accessible web primitives, maintained by WorkOS ([README](https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives)). It's web-only and has nothing for agents.

**Base UI** — Unstyled accessible primitives from the Radix, Floating UI and MUI teams ([README](https://github.com/mui/base-ui)). It's a solid foundation, and Ouro HX is built on it, but on its own it's web-only and has nothing for agents.

**MUI** — A comprehensive React implementation of Material Design, plus MUI X ([README](https://github.com/mui/material-ui)). It's web-only and has no agent model.

**Chakra UI** — Accessible React components, and its README offers an MCP server for Cursor ([README](https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui)). That server helps agents write code, not operate the interface, and it's web-only.

**Fluent UI** — Microsoft's React v9, v8 and Web Components ([README](https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui)). It's mature for Microsoft 365-style web apps, but this repo doesn't cover native platforms or agent-facing contracts.

**Flutter** — One codebase for mobile, web and desktop, rendered with Impeller ([README](https://github.com/flutter/flutter)). Agent UI comes through A2UI/GenUI packages, which are moving off the deprecated `genui` package, so it's a rendering target, not a contract between people and agents. On the web it draws to a canvas, which I see as a trade-off for accessibility and for agents reading the DOM.

**SwiftUI and Apple Human Interface Guidelines** — The best native toolkit for Apple platforms, with accessibility built in ([docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui)). It doesn't run on the web or Android. Ouro's Apple package and A2UI's SwiftUI renderer both build on it.

**Material 3 and Jetpack Compose** — The standard native toolkit for Android, with adaptive layouts and a semantics API ([docs](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/designsystems/material3)). It only covers Android. A2UI's `material3-a2ui` is the most practical way to add agent-generated UI here, and it's the piece I'd use to fill Ouro's Android gap.
